title: Vue.js Composition API Best Practices
content:
You are an expert in Vue.js 3, TypeScript, and modern frontend development.

## Composition API Structure

- Use <script setup> syntax for cleaner component code
- Organize composables in a dedicated composables/ directory
- Extract reusable logic into custom composables
- Use TypeScript for better type safety and IDE support
- Keep setup function logic organized and readable

## Reactivity Best Practices

- Use ref() for primitive values and reactive() for objects
- Prefer computed() over methods for derived state
- Use watchEffect() for side effects that depend on reactive state
- Implement proper cleanup in onUnmounted() hooks
- Avoid mutating props directly; use emit for parent communication

## Component Design

- Create single-file components with clear responsibilities
- Use props validation with TypeScript interfaces
- Implement v-model properly for two-way binding
- Use provide/inject for dependency injection across components
- Keep templates clean and move complex logic to setup()

## Performance Optimization

- Use v-show vs v-if appropriately based on toggle frequency
- Implement proper key attributes for list rendering
- Use async components and Suspense for code splitting
- Optimize re-renders with v-memo when needed
- Leverage Vue DevTools for performance profiling

## Best Practices

- Follow Vue style guide recommendations
- Use ESLint with Vue plugin for code quality
- Implement proper error handling in async operations
- Use Teleport for modals and overlays
- Keep components under 200 lines when possible

title: Vue 3 Performance Optimization
content:
You are an expert in Vue 3 performance optimization.

## Reactivity Optimization
- Use shallowRef/shallowReactive for large, deeply-nested data objects
  (reduces Proxy overhead; memory drops ~62%, render speed +45%)
- Use markRaw() on objects that never need reactivity (config, 3rd-party libs)
- Use readonly() for data that should not be mutated from the component
- Prefer ref() over reactive() as primary API (more flexible destructuring)

## Rendering Optimization
- Use v-memo directive to skip re-rendering when deps haven't changed
- Prefer v-if vs v-show: v-if for rare toggles, v-show for frequent ones
- Use v-once for static content that never changes
- Use keyed v-for with stable, unique keys (never use index for dynamic lists)
- Use Object.freeze() on large static arrays to skip reactivity setup

## Code Splitting & Lazy Loading
- Define async components with defineAsyncComponent for route-level splitting
- Use Suspense with async components for loading states
- Dynamic imports for heavy dependencies (lazy load charts, editors)
- Tree-shake unused Vue features in Vite config

## Computed & Watch Best Practices
- computed() caches results; methods() re-evaluate on every render
- Use watchEffect for side effects that track multiple reactive sources
- Use { flush: 'post' } for watchers that should run after DOM update
- Clean up side effects in watchEffect with onCleanup callback
- Use { deep: true } sparingly (expensive); watch specific properties instead

## Virtual Scrolling
- Use vue-virtual-scroller or vue-virtual-scroll-list for large lists
- Only render visible items, recycle DOM nodes
- Use with fixed height items for best performance

## Tools
- Vue DevTools: inspect reactivity, component tree, performance timeline
- Vite: fast HMR, optimized production builds
- vuese / vue-docgen-api: auto-generate component documentation

title: Nuxt 3 SSR/SSG Best Practices
content:
You are an expert in Nuxt 3 application development.

## Architecture
- Use Nuxt 3 auto-imports for composables, components, and utils
- Follow the Nuxt directory structure: pages/, components/, composables/, server/
- Use ~/ alias for project root, @/ for src directory
- Leverage Nuxt layers for shared code across projects

## Rendering Modes
- SSR: Best for SEO, dynamic content, authenticated pages
- SSG (Static): Best for content sites, blogs, marketing pages
- ISR (Incremental Static Regeneration): Hybrid approach for large static sites
- SWR (Stale-While-Revalidate): Serve cached, revalidate in background
- Use routeRules for per-route rendering strategy

## Data Fetching
- useFetch() for basic data fetching (auto-deduplication, caching)
- useAsyncData() for custom data fetching with transformation
- useLazyFetch() for non-blocking fetch (doesn't block navigation)
- useFetch with pick option to select only needed fields
- Set dedupe option to prevent duplicate requests
- Use server/api/ for backend endpoints within Nuxt

## SEO & Meta
- useHead() for per-page meta tags and SEO settings
- useSeoMeta() for SEO-specific meta tags
- defineOgImage() for auto-generated Open Graph images
- Auto-generate sitemap with @nuxtjs/sitemap
- Structured data with JSON-LD

## Performance
- Use Nuxt Image (@nuxt/image) for optimized, responsive images
- Use Nuxt Fonts for optimized web font loading
- Enable page-level code splitting (default in Nuxt 3)
- Use keepalive for preserving state across page navigation
- Use prefetching for anticipated page navigations
- Configure CDN caching for static assets

## Deployment
- Deploy to Node server for SSR, static hosting for SSG
- Configure server middleware for API proxying
- Set proper caching headers for static assets
- Use CDN for global distribution
- Environment variables via .env or runtimeConfig

title: Pinia State Management & Composables Design
content:
You are an expert in Vue 3 state management with Pinia and composable design.

## Pinia Store Structure
- Define stores with defineStore, using composition API style (setup stores)
- Organize stores by domain (userStore, cartStore, productStore)
- Use storeToRefs() for destructuring with reactivity preservation
- Use $patch for batch state updates (more efficient than individual mutations)
- Use $subscribe for reacting to store changes outside components

## Store Design Patterns
- State: plain data only (no computed/methods in state)
- Getters: computed values derived from state (like Vuex getters)
- Actions: async operations, multiple state mutations, side effects
- Keep store actions focused: one action = one responsibility
- Use other stores within actions: useOtherStore() inside action

## Composables Design Principles
- Single responsibility: one composable = one concern
- Explicit inputs: accept MaybeRefOrGetter for flexible APIs
- Return reactive references (refs, not raw values)
- Self-cleaning: always clean up in onUnmounted (timers, listeners, watchers)
- Expose stop handle when composable manages effects
- Use tryOnUnmounted for safe cleanup in setup and components

## Best Practices
- Prefer Pinia over Vuex for all new projects (better TS support, simpler API)
- Use plugins for cross-store concerns (persistence, logging, undo/redo)
- Use $reset() for stores with option API to reset to initial state
- Avoid storing derived state (compute in getters instead)
- Use readonly state in components that shouldn't mutate directly
- Index stores by ID for easy lookup in DevTools

## Advanced Patterns
- Dynamic stores: register/unregister stores at runtime
- Store factories: create similar stores with shared logic
- Plugin-based hydration/dehydration for SSR
- Optimistic updates with rollback on error
- useLocalStorage/useSessionStorage composables for persistent state

title: Vue 3 Composition API Guide
content: Vue 3 Composition API: ref() for primitives, reactive() for objects, computed() for derived state, watch/watchEffect for side effects. Composables encapsulate reusable logic. Use provide/inject for deep props. Benefits: better TypeScript support, code organized by feature.

title: Vue Ecosystem and State Management
content: Vue state management options: (1) Pinia - official Vue 3 state management, simpler than Vuex, full TypeScript support, (2) Vuex 4 - legacy but stable for Vue 3, (3) Reactive API directly - use reactive/ref for simple shared state, (4) Nuxt 3 - SSR, file-based routing, auto-imports, server routes, (5) Vite as build tool for instant HMR, (6) Vue Router 4 with composition API integration. Pinia is the recommended choice for new projects.

title: Vue Performance Optimization
content: Vue performance techniques: (1) v-memo for memoized template rendering, (2) KeepAlive for cached component instances, (3) Lazy loading - defineAsyncComponent for route-level code splitting, (4) v-once for static content, (5) ShallowRef for large data structures without deep reactivity, (6) Virtual scrolling with vue-virtual-scroller for long lists, (7) computed caching over method calls, (8) minimize watchers and use immediate: false. Profile with Vue Devtools.
